answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph by bounded-length random walks from independently anchored nodes, so repeated links within a sybil cluster do not create independent trust. If the cluster is a hollow region separated by a sparse external cut, its low conductance limits walk flow across that boundary; with capped edge weights and normalized seed mass, this bounds its aggregate voting weight. Min-cut transitivity bounds also prevent a juniper-like chain from turning an oasis of mutual attestations into disproportionate influence.
